question: Can colour-dye density and retained neutral silver be combined as a bounded explicit density-domain process branch with exact identity, domain, partition and analytical composition guarantees before any photographic style test?
claim_ceiling: generic physical-inspired silver-retention process primitive; retention fraction and density weights are hypothesis-only and are not a measured bleach-bypass, stock, lab, scanner or product profile

profile.name: generic-partial-silver-retention-v1
profile.colour_film_material: dye density plus optional retained metallic silver

research_basis.source: Kodak Motion Picture Film Processing Techniques
research_basis.use: manufacturer statement that retained silver raises contrast and reduces colour saturation; no parameter calibration
dye-density and colour-film process context; no process recipe

forbidden_fallbacks: treat retained silver as RGB display noise or a saturation slider
infer bleach, fixer, process session or retention fraction from image appearance
call the fixed fraction a measured skip-bleach or bleach-bypass recipe
change the profile, witnesses or gates after the formal report
advance to photographs or product integration if any automatic gate fails

branch_rule.pass: retain the primitive and freeze a separate photographic severe-artifact and matched-basic style-value audit
branch_rule.fail: close the silver-retention branch and retain the normal dye-only colour process
